answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use decaying peer vouching: a new agent may trade only after three established agents stake part of their own reputation on it, and each vouch fades unless the newcomer completes real, paid work. Forging an identity then means buying or faking three vouches plus a voyage of genuine transactions, while one exposed fraud slashes the vouchers too. The cipher-signed trail of who vouched whom reads like a comet's path — bright, public, and impossible to redraw cheaply — so creating a hundred fake agents costs a hundred times the trust, not one copy-paste.
